newsitem.title: USA: U.S., Japan set new insurance pact deadline.
newsitem.headline: U.S., Japan set new insurance pact deadline.

text.p: The United States and Japan have agreed to try to settle a long-running dispute over the insurance market in Japan by the end of this year, Acting U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky said Tuesday.
Japanese officials announced the interim agreement late Monday night.

Barshefsky said the agreement will control entry by subsidiaries of major Japanese life and non-life insurance companies into the so-called third sector, which has been a profitable niche for foreign firms.

The Japanese subsidiaries will not be allowed to enter the third sector before the end of this year while the two nations negotiate an overall agreement to avoid "radical change" in the third sector and to provide substantial deregulation of the life and non-life insurance sectors, Barshefsky said.
The interim agreement calls for some deregulation but significantly more will be needed to resolve the issue, she said.
Barshefsky said the insurance agreement should be viewed as an "interim" pact and that it bars entry into the third sector until an overall comprehensive agreement is reached.
"Subsidiaries are barred ... from third sector entry until we reach a comprehensive agreement," Barshefsky said at a press briefing.
She said that until that time, there would be no entry into the third sector that the United States would tolerate, and if it was attempted, "we will absolutely take action."
The so-called third sector niche insurance market covers areas such as personal accident, sickness and nursing care.
In the interim pact, Japan agreed to allow sales of automobile insurance directly to consumers by mail or telephone, the trade representative said.
Barshefsky called that a "down payment" by Japan on primary sector deregulation.
She said U.S. companies will be able to begin direct marketing of automobile insurance immediately.
